macro_context.market_sentiment: Mixed but near record highs — S&P 500 set new all-time record on May 6 (7,365.12), but pulled back on May 7 (-0.38%) as oil prices rebounded and Iran peace deal optimism faded. Tech (Nvidia, Microsoft, Tesla) showed relative strength. AI/semiconductor earnings beats from AMD and Supermicro fueled optimism early in the week.
macro_context.fed_outlook: Fed held benchmark funds rate steady at 3.5%–3.75% at its April 28-29 meeting (Powell's final meeting as Chair) with an unusual 8-4 dissent. SEP projects one rate cut in 2026. Statement cites elevated inflation partly from rising global energy prices, signaling no imminent easing. Next FOMC meeting expected June 2026.
macro_context.geopolitical: Ongoing US-Iran war is the dominant geopolitical risk — disrupting energy markets, threatening Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes, and pushing oil prices higher. Markets rallied on May 6 on reports the US and Iran may be nearing a peace agreement, but gains partially reversed May 7 as talks remained uncertain. NATO posture in Greenland also intensifying as a secondary concern.

STX stock moved up 6.85% on May 5 following earnings beat and AI demand surge; stock up ~147% YTD and near 52-week highs

analyst_consensus.recent_changes: Post-Q3 earnings upgrades: Mizuho raised PT to $875 (Outperform); Morgan Stanley raised PT to $767 (Overweight) and named STX its #1 IT Hardware stock; Barclays raised PT to $750 (Overweight). BofA and Cantor Fitzgerald had raised PTs to $700 ahead of earnings. Earlier in 2026: Susquehanna upgraded from Negative to Neutral with $280 PT (Jan 16, 2026) — now significantly below current stock price (~$787). Consensus: Buy from ~20-23 analysts.

web_context.competitor_activity: Western Digital (WDC) surged 60% in April after its own earnings beat ($2.13 EPS vs $1.93 expected), positioning as a pure HDD play. Both STX and WDC have confirmed their 2026 production quotas are essentially sold out, underscoring the AI storage supercycle demand. Toshiba (private) is pursuing a cautious MAMR-first strategy before moving to HAMR. Seagate maintains a differentiated HAMR technology leadership position, already shipping 44TB drives and targeting 100TB-class products. The HDD oligopoly (just 3 players) means strong pricing power for all three.
